body:
## Problem

The codebase has mixed concerns throughout. The aggregator service's `sources/` directory contains 4 source adapters that directly use `axios`, raw HTTP calls, and filesystem I/O intermixed with business logic (backoff, normalization, staleness checks). The API service mixes Express request handling with caching logic, WebSocket broadcasting, and data serialization in route handlers. This makes the system impossible to unit-test without mocking infrastructure, impossible to swap frameworks, and impossible to reason about domain logic in isolation.

## Requirements

- **Full DDD with tactical patterns** — Redesign the domain layer with: Aggregates (PriceFeed, OracleSource), Value Objects (Price, Timestamp, Deviation, QualityScore), Domain Events (PriceUpdated, SourceStale, DeviationDetected), Repository interfaces, Domain Services, and Factory methods. No domain class may depend on anything outside the domain layer.
- **Hexagonal architecture with port adapters** — Define port interfaces in the domain layer for: PricePersistencePort, SourceFetchingPort, ClockPort, EventBusPort, LoggingPort. Implement adapters in infrastructure layer for: filesystem, HTTP (axios), WebSocket (ws library), Soroban RPC, Prometheus, Winston. The domain layer must be buildable and testable with ZERO infrastructure dependencies.
- **Runtime-adapter hot-swapping** — The adapter resolution must support runtime configuration changes. Switching from filesystem persistence to PostgreSQL persistence must require only a config change and a restart, not code changes. Implement a service locator or DI container with dynamic binding.
- **Multi-tenant isolation** — The domain model must support multi-tenancy at the aggregate level. Each tenant has isolated PriceFeed aggregates, source configurations, and staleness thresholds. Tenant context is propagated through domain events.
- **Anti-corruption layer for each external system** — Build ACLs for: Soroban RPC (converts between Stellar-specific types and domain types), Chainlink/Redstone/Band/Reflector APIs (normalizes different JSON structures), Express HTTP (maps between HTTP concepts and domain commands). These ACLs should be independently testable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Domain layer extracted with zero framework/infrastructure imports (pure TypeScript)
- [ ] All 5 port interfaces defined and implemented by infrastructure adapters
- [ ] DI container supports dynamic adapter binding at startup
- [ ] Domain layer has 100% test coverage without any mocks (real domain logic tested directly)
- [ ] Multi-tenant PriceFeed isolation verified with integration tests
- [ ] Anti-corruption layers for Soroban, external oracles, Express HTTP
- [ ] Runtime adapter hot-swapping demonstrated with config change
- [ ] All existing tests (63) continue to pass after refactor
title: Full DDD + hexagonal architecture with hot-swappable adapters and multi-tenant isolation
